_about: Rolling Edition subject taxonomy: areas (top level) and skills (what books are cataloged under). This file is the source of truth. IDs are permanent; labels can change. Wikipedia titles anchor each term; fill Wikidata IDs with `re-check wikidata --write`.

areas.label: Artificial intelligence
areas.description: Building applications on language models and other AI systems: prompting, retrieval, agents, evaluation.

areas.label: Machine learning
areas.description: Training, evaluating and improving models from data.

areas.label: Search and recommendation
areas.description: Finding and ranking the right items for a query or a person: search engines, recommenders, ranking.

areas.label: Data engineering
areas.description: Moving, storing and preparing data reliably: pipelines, warehouses, streams, quality.

areas.label: Data science
areas.description: Learning from data to make decisions: statistics, experiments, causal inference, visualization.

areas.label: MLOps
areas.description: Running models in production: deployment, monitoring, evaluation over time.

skills.label: Large language models
skills.description: How language models work and how to build with them.

skills.label: Prompt engineering
skills.description: Designing and testing the instructions a model receives.

skills.label: Retrieval-augmented generation
skills.description: Grounding a model's answers in retrieved documents.

skills.label: AI agents
skills.description: Systems where a model plans and uses tools to reach a goal.

skills.label: LLM evaluation
skills.description: Test sets, graders, regression suites and monitoring for LLM applications.

skills.label: Natural language processing
skills.description: Working with text: representation, classification, extraction.

skills.label: Deep learning
skills.description: Neural networks and how to train them.

skills.label: Feature engineering
skills.description: Turning raw data into inputs a model can learn from.

skills.label: Model evaluation
skills.description: Measuring whether a model is good enough, offline and online.

skills.label: Model monitoring
skills.description: Watching models in production for drift, errors and regressions.

skills.label: Learning to rank
skills.description: Training models that order results.

skills.label: Search relevance
skills.description: Making search return the right results, and knowing that it does.

skills.label: Search evaluation
skills.description: Relevance judgments, metrics such as NDCG, and online tests for search.

skills.label: Semantic search
skills.description: Search by meaning with embeddings.

skills.label: Vector databases
skills.description: Storing and querying embeddings at scale.

skills.label: Recommender systems
skills.description: Suggesting items to people: candidate generation, ranking, cold start.

skills.label: Data pipelines and ETL
skills.description: Extracting, transforming and loading data on a schedule or on demand.

skills.label: Stream processing
skills.description: Processing data continuously as it arrives.

skills.label: Data warehousing
skills.description: Modeling and storing data for analysis.

skills.label: Data quality
skills.description: Testing and monitoring data so it can be trusted.

skills.label: Data governance
skills.description: Knowing what data you hold, who owns it, where it flows and who may see it.

skills.label: Experimentation and A/B testing
skills.description: Designing and reading controlled experiments.

skills.label: Causal inference
skills.description: Estimating effects when you can't run an experiment, and when you can.

skills.label: Data visualization
skills.description: Charts that show the truth in data.

skills.label: Time series forecasting
skills.description: Predicting values that change over time.
